He was born in [[Orange, New Jersey]] and raised in [[East Massapequa, New York]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.stamfordadvocate.com/news/article/UConn-s-Price-cleared-to-play-114558.php|title=UConn's Price cleared to play}} He is the son of former NBA player [[Tony Price (basketball)|Tony Price]].[http://www.cbssports.com/columns/story/11523555 They'll never Penn another Cinderella story like the Quakers']. Knapp, Gwen (March 19, 2009). CBS Sports. ==High school career== Price attended [[Amityville Memorial High School]], where he led the Warriors to three straight Long Island Championships and state titles in his sophomore and junior seasons. As a junior (2003) he averaged 25.4 points, seven rebounds, five assists and three steals. His numbers continued to increase as a senior; he averaged 28.5 points and eight rebounds. He finished his three-year career with 130 career three-pointers and 1,394 career points. He was a two-time Newsday Suffolk County Player of the Year.{{Cite web|url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=5154&Sport=2#bio|title=A. J. Price - Yahoo! Sports}} Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Price was listed as the No. 7 point guard and the No. 32 player in the nation in 2004.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-A.J.-Price-5154;_ylt=AkRwdCDsBk6qPkAHzIpbOOjXO5B4 A. J. Price Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Price chose [[University of Connecticut|UConn]] over [[Florida State University|Florida State]], [[University of Kansas|Kansas]] and [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]].{{cite web|url=http://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewprospect.asp?pr_key=5154&Sport=2 |title=A. J. Price Profile - Basketball Recruiting |publisher=Basketballrecruiting.rivals.com |access-date=2009-06-14}} He missed his freshman (2004–05) season after a life-threatening battle with [[Arteriovenous malformation|AVM]], which caused bleeding in his brain.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2204906|title=UConn's Price pursues deal to erase criminal record|date=October 27, 2005|website=ESPN.com}} He underwent radio-surgery treatment in February 2005 and spent more than 14 months recovering from his illness.{{cite news|last=Brady |first=Erik |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/bigeast/2005-01-12-price-sidelined_x.htm |title=67k |publisher=Usatoday.com |date=2005-01-12 |access-date=2009-06-14}} It was not until May 2006 that he received clearance from his doctors to return to the court. However, Price was suspended by the university for the 2005–06 academic semester due to violations of the University Student Code of Conduct.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2207100|title=Connecticut suspends Price for entire 2005-06 season|date=October 28, 2005|website=ESPN.com}} He was arrested, along with fellow basketball player [[Marcus Williams (basketball, born 1985)|Marcus Williams]] in August 2005 on charges of trying to sell stolen laptops. He pleaded not guilty to larceny charges.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2146860|title=UConn guard Price pleads not guilty to larceny charge|date=August 30, 2005|website=ESPN.com}} Price was not permitted to take classes during the Fall 2005 semester, but returned to classes in the Spring 2006 semester.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=2224935 |title=UConn guard Price gets probation in laptop case - Men's College Basketball - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2005-11-15 |access-date=2009-06-14}} He returned to the court for the 2006–07 season as a sophomore. He appeared in all 31 games, starting at point guard in 23 contests. For the season he averaged 9.4 points per game with 113 assists and 37 steals to his credit in 23.9 minutes per game. In the 2007–08 season, Price started all 33 games at point guard and was UConn's second leading scorer. He won many awards and was named to the U.S. Basketball Writers Association's All-America Team. He was also a unanimous selection to the First Team All-BIG EAST squad and selected as USBWA District Player of the Year and member of All-District First Team, named a finalist for the John R. Wooden Award, and was chosen as one of ten finalists for the USBWA Player of the Year Award, the Oscar Robertson Trophy and named to the NABC All-District 1 First Team. In the first round of the 2008 NCAA Tournament against San Diego Price played nine minutes before tearing his left [[anterior cruciate ligament]]. The team would go on to lose the game by one point in overtime. The next season 2008–09 was the best season for Price. Coming off the ACL injury he was the Huskies' leading scorer with 14.7 points a game and was critical in their run to the final four. In a game versus Gonzaga he hit a falling down three-pointer to force the game into overtime.{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283552250&campaign=rss&source=ESPNHeadlines |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081223051543/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283552250&campaign=rss&source=ESPNHeadlines |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 23, 2008 |title=Connecticut Huskies vs. Gonzaga Bulldogs - Recap - December 20, 2008 - ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2008-12-20 |access-date=2009-06-14}} In the [[2009 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] he was named the most outstanding player in the West Region, but the Huskies fell in the semi-finals to the Michigan State Spartans.{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/draft/players/524942|title=A.J. Price Wizards.jpg|thumb|Price with the Wizards|right|upright]] Price was selected in the second round of the [[2009 NBA draft]] at number 52 overall by the [[Indiana Pacers]] on June 25, 2009. Midway through the 2009–10 season, Price, along with [[Earl Watson]], moved ahead of [[T. J. Ford]] on the team's depth chart. In December, Watson became the starter and Price became the primary backup point guard. In the 2011–12 season, Price backed up [[Darren Collison]] when [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]] was injured; however, when the Pacers acquired [[Leandro Barbosa]], he received fewer minutes. On July 24, 2012, Price signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-sign-aj-price |title=Wizards Sign A.J. Price | work=NBA.com | date=July 24, 2012 | access-date=July 24, 2012}} On September 30, 2013, Price signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14380 |title=Timberwolves add A.J. Price to training camp roster |access-date=2013-10-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705072838/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14380 |archive-date=2017-07-05 |url-status=dead }} On April 3, 2014, he was waived by the Timberwolves.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/press-release-wolves-waive-guard-aj-price|title=Press Release: Wolves Waive Guard A.J. Price|website=www.nba.com}} On September 26, 2014, Price signed with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/news/training-camp-roster-2014|title=Cavaliers Announce 2014-15 Training Camp Roster|website=[[NBA.com]] }} On November 1, 2014, he was waived by the Cavaliers before playing in a regular season game for them.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-price-141101|title=Cavs Waive A.J. Price|website=www.nba.com}} On November 6, 2014, Price signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]] to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Indiana had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-aj-price|title=Pacers Sign A.J. Price|website=www.nba.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11831195/indiana-pacers-look-sign-aj-price|title=Pacers sign Price, give up on Israel's Mekel|date=November 6, 2014|website=ESPN.com}} On November 28, 2014, he was waived by the Pacers.{{cite news|title=Pacers Waive A.J. Price|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-aj-price|access-date=November 28, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 28, 2014}} Two days later, he was claimed off waivers by the Cavaliers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/price-waivers-cherry-waive-141130|title=Cavs Claim A.J. Price off waivers, Waive Will Cherry|website=www.nba.com}} On January 7, 2015, he was waived again by Cavaliers.{{cite news|title=Cavaliers Waive A.J. Price|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-price-150107|access-date=January 7, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2015}} On March 21, he signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]] and made his debut for the team later that night, recording 2 points, 1 rebound and 1 assist in a 117–102 win over the Houston Rockets.{{Cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2015/3/21/8269355/phoenix-suns-new-backup-pg-a-j-price-fits-in-many-ways|title=The Price is right|first=Dave|last=King|date=March 21, 2015|website=Bright Side Of The Sun}}{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150321/PHXHOU/gameinfo.html |title=Bledsoe scores career-best 34 as Suns beat Rockets 117-102 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-03-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630065222/http://www.nba.com/games/20150321/PHXHOU/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2015-06-30 |url-status=dead }} He was not retained by the Suns following the expiration of his 10-day contract on March 31.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-jerel-mcneal-10-day-contract|title=Suns Sign Jerel McNeal to 10-Day Contract|website=www.nba.com}} In September 2015, Price signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].[https://twitter.com/IAmDPick/status/642455071515639808 Source: NBA veteran guard A.J. His father Tony was a standout basketball performer at the [[University of Pennsylvania]], helping the team advance to the [[1979 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament]] and eventually into the Final Four.
